name: Myeloschisis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Myeloschisis

criteria.description: Presence of an open neural tube defect with exposed spinal cord tissue without overlying skin
MRI or ultrasound evidence of spinal cord malformation with absence of skin covering
Congenital lower limb motor and sensory deficits consistent with spinal cord exposure
Presence of associated anomalies such as hydrocephalus or Chiari II malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of open spinal cord defect with exposed neural tissue confirmed by imaging plus clinical neurological deficits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; prenatal ultrasound may detect the defect.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exposed open spinal cord without skin covering
pathognomonic.notes: Visible at birth as an open lesion on the back

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of deep tendon reflexes below lesion level
searchTerms: no deep tendon reflexes below damage

common.notes: Neurogenic bladder and bowel due to spinal cord involvement
Often associated with Chiari II malformation

searchTerms: brain tissue herniation at skull base

occasional.symptomName: Skin ulceration or infection at lesion site
searchTerms: ulcers or infections on skin lesion

rare.symptomName: Lower limb edema due to venous insufficiency

imaging: MRI showing open spinal cord defect with absent skin covering
MRI evidence of Chiari II malformation and hydrocephalus
genetic: No specific gene identified; multifactorial etiology including folate metabolism genes
other: Physical examination revealing open spinal lesion
Neurological examination showing motor and sensory deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Intact skin covering over spinal defect
Usually asymptomatic or mild neurological signs
Cystic sac containing meninges but no exposed spinal cord

redFlags: Open spinal cord lesion with risk of infection
Signs of increased intracranial pressure due to hydrocephalus
references: Wheeler PG, et al. Neural Tube Defects. In: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics, 21st Edition. 2020.
Moore KL, Persaud TVN. The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology. 11th Edition. 2015.
